synopsis: XLD is an on-road benchmark introduced in a June 2024 preprint, with a 2025 v3 using synthetic CARLA data; Chapter 7 cites it as evidence of a significant neural-reconstruction gap at cross-lane viewpoint offsets of 1–4 m [f4001, f5515]. Reported 3DGS PSNR fell from 30.87 dB at zero lateral shift to 23.26, 22.01 and 19.17 dB at shifts of 1, 2 and 4 m, respectively [f4001]. At 4 m, EmerNeRF achieved the best PSNR, 24.80 dB, and EmerNeRF and UC-NeRF held up better than the 3DGS variant PVG, creating tension with industry preference for 3DGS editability [f4002, f4329]. Three cameras substantially reduced the reported drop compared with one camera, indicating that camera configuration affects the benchmark outcome [f4024]. Across chapters, XLD supports caution about off-trajectory neural re-simulation despite proponents’ enthusiasm; its findings align with other benchmarks on viewpoint-change degradation, but the cited evidence remains on-road or urban rather than off-road [f5785, f4289].

relations.note: Measured PSNR degradation substantiates the cross-lane reconstruction gap.
XLD lateral-shift measurements support the broader cross-benchmark degradation finding.
The significant cross-lane gap grounds XLD authors’ caution about off-trajectory re-simulation.
Consistent independent benchmark findings reinforce the stated disagreement over neural re-simulation.
EmerNeRF’s best 4 m PSNR supports the reported NeRF advantage over PVG.
Three-camera results qualify the gap by showing camera configuration can reduce degradation.
Adds camera-count sensitivity to the reported lateral-view degradation.
